digest:
- NYC lawmakers are weighing a bill to require direct employment of Amazon delivery workers instead of DSPs, threatening to remove insurable commercial auto policies from the open broker market [1].
- GEODIS reports final-mile delivery prices up 10.5% YoY and record diesel highs, squeezing fleet profitability and making telematics-driven premium savings critical for target Amazon DSP and courier fleets [2].
- Walmart's surging sub-30-minute delivery volumes in Q3 increase last-mile fleet exposure and rush-induced driving risk, strengthening the commercial need for telematics risk selection [3].
- Major motor carriers are shifting AI dashcams and telematics toward proactive driver coaching and crash prevention, validating market demand for Nirvana's thesis that behavioral coaching reduces loss frequency [5].
- Forge Insurance integrated ePayPolicy with its Majesco policy administration system, showcasing competing commercial auto carriers streamlining digital payment workflows for wholesale broker distribution [9].

new.title: NY City Lawmakers Weigh Overhaul of Amazon Delivery Worker Bill
new.summary: New York City lawmakers are considering revisions to a bill requiring Amazon to directly employ delivery workers rather than contracting them through DSPs.
new.evidence_quote: New York City lawmakers are in discussions to modify a mandate that would require Amazon.com Inc. to directly hire thousands of delivery workers
new.implication: Direct-hire mandates threaten the Amazon DSP business model; converting DSPs into corporate employees would remove insurable commercial auto policies from the open broker market.

new.implication: High final-mile operating costs squeeze fleet profitability, making telematics-driven risk management and premium savings critical for target Amazon DSP and courier fleets.
